conventions: Gentilic הַתְּקוֹעִית recast as 'of Tekoa': the gentilic takes 'of Tekoa' as its own unit, headed on Tekoa, and its article is unrepresented because the ASV writes no 'the' for it (14.4, 14.9).

Oath formula חַי־יְהוָה / חֵי־נַפְשְׁךָ followed by אִם: the adjective takes 'As … liveth' (rule 55) and the oath's אִם is what carries the negation the ASV writes for it — 'not' in 14.11, 'none' in 14.19 — so it is aligned to that word and not left unrepresented.

לֵאמֹר rendered 'to say' (rather than 'saying') gives the written 'to' to the לְ under rule 52's written-word sentence; rule 27's unrepresented לְ governs only the bare 'saying' rendering, which stands in the same verse (s010) and is marked that way.

Vocative אֲדֹנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ → 'My lord, O king': lord takes its own word with 'My' on the suffix, the article is unrepresented, and מֶלֶךְ takes 'O king' (14.9, 14.22); where the same phrase is not vocative ('my lord the king', 14.12, 14.15, 14.17, 14.18, 14.19) the article takes 'the' as usual.
report: Read every candidate group and the six added units end to end. No construction is analysed two ways without the ASV licensing the difference: the rectum-vs-object contrasts (אָח, אָמָה, רֹאשׁ, מַלְאָךְ, אָדוֹן, שִׁפְחָה 'of X' vs bare) follow rule 19; the directive he takes to/unto/on as written (rule 32); the lexical waws (Now, So, Then, but, therefore, even, or, for, that, and when, and so) are all read off the ASV under rules 14 and 55; apodosis waws are unrepresented in every verse that has one (14.4, 10, 26, 32, 33); article + demonstrative, agreement articles, vocative 'O king' with its article unrepresented, the gentilic 'of Tekoa', the possessive recasting of construct chains, and the אֲדֹנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ formula are handled identically wherever they recur.

Single-verse judgments that carry a named competing reading and were left standing: 14.5 מַה־לָּךְ → What aileth thee (aileth on the predicate לְ); 14.10 יֹסִיף עוֹד → 'any more' fused; 14.19 existential אִשׁ → 'can'; 14.25 'for his beauty' kept whole on יָפֶה (the 'his' could instead resume Absalom under rule 25 or be added under rule 18's closing sentence); 14.31 אֲשֶׁר־לִי → 'my' fused on the predicate לְ under rule 49; 14.7 'and so' as a rule-55 pair. None is a cross-verse split, and each note already names the alternative.

BSB disagreements are all documented convention differences: articles, waws, object markers and silenced prepositions; the resumed object suffix of 14.6 (the ASV renders the object once via אֶת־הָאֶחָד); the dative לוֹ suffix of 14.33 (the ASV's 'himself' is the Hishtaphel's reflexive, not the dative); the repeated יָמִים and its לַ in 14.26 (rule 22 distributive repetition); the אֲנִי of 14.32 dissolved by the infinitival recasting; the deictic זֶה of 14.2 and the paragogic he of 14.4. None is a genuine error.

Conventions recorded for the four chapter-wide judgments that are not restatements of the contract. No promotions or amendments: the chapter taught nothing the contract lacks, and the one tension noticed (rule 27's categorical 'no realization' for לֵאמֹר against 14.32's written 'to say') is recorded as a convention rather than promoted, since no corpus evidence on לֵאמֹר → to say was supplied.
